423025.title: Roma
423025.description: The capital of the Roman Republic and Empire.

148127.title: Massalia/Massilia
148127.description: Massalia/Massilia (modern Marseille, France) was founded by Phocaean Greeks ca. 600 B.C. as a trading outpost. Massalia, in turn, established its own secondary colonies. During the Punic Wars Massalia, was allied to Rome and, following the sacking of Carthage in 146 B.C., the settlement enjoyed increased economic vitality.

246349.title: Col. Tarraco
246349.description: An Iberian site in contact with Greek and Phoenician merchants that became a major Roman center from the third century BC onward.
246349.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 25 G4 Col. Tarraco

246369.title: Dertosa/Hibera Iulia Ilercavonia
246369.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 25 F5 Dertosa/Hibera Iulia Ilercavonia
246369.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 25 F5 Dertosa/Hibera Iulia Ilercavonia

266021.title: Saguntum/Arse
266021.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 27 E2 Saguntum/Arse

265883.title: Ebusus
265883.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 27 G3 Ebusus

266090.title: Valentia
266090.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 27 E2 Valentia

265880.title: Dianium/Hemeroskopeion
265880.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 27 F3 Dianium/Hemeroskopeion

265849.title: Carthago Nova/Col. Urbs Iulia
265849.description: Carthago Nova/Col. Urbs Iulia (modern Cartagena, Spain) was originally an indigenous settlement that was subsequently refounded first as a Punic site Qart Hadasht ("New City") in 228 BC and later as a Roman city.
265849.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 27 E4 Carthago Nova/Col. Urbs Iulia

265823.title: Basti
265823.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 27 C4 Basti

265762.title: Abdera
265762.description: An ancient Phoenician port settlement at modern Adra on the southern Spanish coast that was continually inhabited through the end of the Roman period.

265765.title: Acci/Col. Iulia Gemella
265765.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 27 B4 Acci/Col. Iulia Gemella
265765.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 27 B4 Acci/Col. Iulia Gemella

265963.title: Malaca
265963.description: A Roman city of Baetica that was perhaps founded by the Carthaginians in the fifth century BC. Modern Malaga, on the Mediterranean coast of Spain.

256063.title: Carteia/Calpe/Karpessos
256063.description: A Phoenician and Roman town in Spain located on the Bay of Gibraltar. The site played a strategic role in the Punic Wars, and was given the rights of a Latin colony in 171 BC.

256128.title: Corduba/Col. Patricia
256128.description: Corduba/Col. Patricia (modern Córdoba, Andalusia) is an ancient site where prehistoric, Punic, Roman, Visigothic, and Muslim phases of occupation are known. The city's historic center was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.
256128.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 26 F4 Corduba/Col. Patricia

255996.title: Astigi/Col. Augusta Firma
255996.description: Now the modern Ecija on the Genil river, Astigi was the capital of one of the four conventus of Baetica and became an Augustan colony after 27 B.C.
255996.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 26 E4 Astigi/Col. Augusta Firma

256210.title: Hispalis/Col. Romula
256210.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 26 E4 Hispalis/Col. Romula

256193.title: (H)Asta/Col. Hasta Regia/Ligystine?
256193.description: An ancient town near Jerez de la Frontera, which belonged to the Conventus Hispalensis.
256193.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 26 D5 (H)Asta/Col. Hasta Regia/Ligystine?

256177.title: Gadeira/Gades/Col. Augusta Gaditana
256177.description: Gadeira/Gades/Col. Augusta Gaditana (modern Cadiz, Spain) is an ancient city of Spain and one of the oldest continuously occupied cities of Europe. Its origins may be Phoenician (Gadir (Phoenician: גדר)).
256177.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 26 D5 Gadeira/Gades/Col. Augusta Gaditana

462503.title: Syracusae/Syrakousai
462503.description: An important ancient city on the island of Sicily.

314921.title: Carthago
314921.description: The ancient city of Carthage, located in modern Tunis (Tunisia). Carthage engaged the Roman state in a series of wars conventionally referred to as the Punic Wars by scholars.

315248.title: Utica
315248.description: A Punic center located west of Carthage.

324716.title: Hadrumetum/Iustinianopolis
324716.description: Hadrumetum/Iustinianopolis was an important ancient port in North Africa. Founded by the Phoenicians, the site pre-dated Carthage. Under Roman administration, the site prospered, and Trajan assigned it colonial status as Colonia Concordia Ulpia Trajana Augusta Frugifera Hadrumetina.

324827.title: Thapsus
324827.description: An ancient settlement and port, located at modern Ras Dimass in the Tunisian municipality of Bekalta (Monastir). Habitation at the site dates to at least the 6th century BCE and continued through the Byzantine and into the Islamic period, but it appears that the main settlement itself relocated to Bekalta in medieval times.

324835.title: Thysdrus
324835.description: Thysdrus (modern El Djem, Tunisia) was a Punic and Roman city of North Africa. It flourished in the second century A.D. and built its massive amphitheater in the third century. After an abortive revolt in A.D. 238, the city was destroyed by soldiers loyal to Maximinus Thrax.

344380.title: Gigthis
344380.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 35 C1 Gigthis

344282.title: Abrotonum/Sabratha
344282.description: The westernmost of the "three cities" of Tripolis, Abrotonum/Sabratha was founded ca. 500 B.C. by the Phoenicians. The city was part of the Numidian Kingdom of Massinissa before becoming a Roman city.

344456.title: Oea
344456.description: Phoenicians established Oea in the seventh century B.C., and it later became a Roman–Berber colony. Modern-day Tripoli, Libya.

344448.title: Neapolis/Lepcis Magna
344448.description: Originally a Phoenician colony founded ca. 1100 B.C., Lepcis Magna became a prominent Roman city and birthplace of the emperor Septimius Severus.
344448.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 35 G2 Neapolis/Lepcis Magna

363959.title: Euphranta/Macomades
363959.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 37 B1 Euphranta/Macomades

373757.title: Berenice
373757.description: Berenice was a coastal city of western Cyrenaica, located at modern Benghazi in Libya. Founded in the third century BCE, it replaced the earlier Greek colony of Eusperides, which had been centered a short distance to the northeast. Berenice was named in honor of Berenice of Cyrene, the queen of Ptolemy III Euergetes.

373736.title: Arsinoe/Taucheira
373736.description: Arsinoe/Taucheira (modern Tocra) may have originally been a Greek foundation that was part of Pentapolis of Cyrenaica. It eventually became a Roman colony and, by the time of Justinian, was fortified.

373750.title: Barke
373750.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 38 B1 Barke

373879.title: Ptolemais/Barkes Limen
373879.description: An ancient capital of Cyrenaica, Ptolemais was probably named after Ptolemy III Euergetes. The city was founded in either the seventh or sixth century BC.
373879.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 38 B1 Ptolemais/Barkes Limen

373732.title: Apollonia/Sozousa
373732.description: Apollonia was an ancient city in the Cyrenaica and a port of Cyrene. The city was one of the five cities of the Libyan Pentapolis in Cyrenaica.

373778.title: Cyrene
373778.description: An ancient Greek city founded in eastern Libya ca. 630 B.C., Cyrene later became part of the Roman Empire (ca. 74 B.C.). The site was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1982.

442509.title: Brundisium/Brentesion
442509.description: A Greek and Roman port, terminus of the Via Appia.

481818.title: Dyrr(h)achium/Epidamnos
481818.description: A city founded in 627 B.C. by colonists from Corinth and Kerkyra.

481728.title: Apollonia
481728.description: Ancient Greek trade colony which developed into an independent polis, and later a Roman city, in southern Illyria

491741.title: Thessalonica
491741.description: A city of northern Greece founded by Cassander of Macedon ca. 315 BCE; an important center of the Roman and Late Antique worlds.

491687.title: Pella/Diokletianoupolis
491687.description: Capital of the Kingdom of Macedonia.

579885.title: Athenae
579885.description: A major Greek city-state and the principal city of Attika. Modern Athens in Greece.

599612.title: Ephesus/Arsinoe(ia)
599612.description: Ephesus/Arsinoe(ia) was the most important ancient metropolis of Ionian Asia Minor.

590030.title: Rhodos (settlement)
590030.description: A settlement on the island of Rhodes.

639042.title: Patara/Arsinoe
639042.description: Patara/Arsinoe was an ancient maritime center of southwest Lycia.

639051.title: Phaselis
639051.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 65 E4 Phaselis

648789.title: Tarsus/Antiochia ad Cydnum
648789.description: An important city and river port on the Cydnus river located in Cilicia Pedias.
648789.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 66 F3 Tarsus/Antiochia ad Cydnum

658381.title: Antiochia/Theoupolis
658381.description: A city founded ca. 300 BC by Seleucus I Nicator, a successor of Alexander the Great. Antioch was a great trading center and numbered as one of the four cities of the Syrian tetrapolis. Justinian I renamed the city 'Theoupolis' in the sixth century AD.

678437.title: Tyrus/Col. Septimia Severa
678437.description: The ancient city of Tyre (modern es-Sur on the coast of Lebanon). A UNESCO World Heritage Site, in part because of its "important archaeological remains, mainly from Roman times."
678437.provenance: Barrington Atlas: BAtlas 69 B3 Tyrus/Col. Septimia Severa

678010.title: Ake/Ptolemais
678010.description: The Phoenician city of Akko was re-founded by Ptolemy II Philadelphos from ca. 285-246 B.C.

678121.title: Dor(a)
678121.description: A coastal settlement of Phoenicia, now Tel Dor, to the south of Haifa.

687902.title: Gaza
687902.description: An important ancient settlement on the coast of Palestine.

727192.title: Pelusium
727192.description: Pelusium was a fortified ancient city located at the mouth of the eastern-most branch of the Nile river. Its ruins, now land-locked and located approximately 30km southeast of Port Said, are known as Tell Farama.

727070.title: Alexandria
727070.description: The ancient port city in Egypt's Nile Delta, founded by Alexander the Great in 332/331 BCE.
